headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent can write broad workspace data while the paired content-writing repo has no isolation or runtime controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B. B can read and write Repl workspace files, so only a manual copy/paste or file handoff bridge exists. That makes prompt injection possible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to the content B consumes.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B's prompt or workspace files
IF B is instructed to treat file contents as instructions
mitigations: Keep A outputs in a separate review document
Require B to summarize before acting on pasted text
Prefix imported text as untrusted data
Use a fixed prompt template that forbids instruction following from pasted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress plus filesystem access. A is a docs-only repository with no runtime surfaces, so it is not itself a leak source, but the pair still creates a workspace where sensitive B data can be exposed through ordinary file handling. The interaction is plausible in default Replit workflows, though not directly evidenced for A.
conditions: IF B opens or writes files containing secrets or deployment config
IF those files are later copied into external tools or logs
mitigations: Store secrets only in the Replit Secrets store
Review workspace files before sharing outputs
Disable unnecessary file exports
Rotate any exposed keys immediately
Use a redaction checklist before copying text out

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or concurrency capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable state. B can write the filesystem and modify git state, and Replit workspaces persist across sessions, so conflicts can arise if multiple B instances or external edits touch the same repo. Because A is inert, the conflict is one-sided but still real for B's shared mutable workspace.
conditions: IF two B sessions edit the same Repl files or git branch
IF an operator edits the workspace while B is running
mitigations: Use one active B session per workspace
Commit or stash before starting another edit cycle
Lock the branch name in advance
Review git diff before each save
Move parallel work into separate Repls

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can supply content that B may treat as authoritative, but A is only a content-writing repo and B is a coding agent with action-taking authority in the Repl. The main risk is B turning unverified A output into code, config, or deployment changes. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, so uncertainty pushes the rating up from low to medium.
conditions: IF A-generated text is pasted into B as requirements or facts
IF B applies that text without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Require B to cite source files before acting
Add a human approval step for code or deployment changes
Ask B to restate assumptions before execution
Keep A outputs in a separate notes file marked untrusted
Run a diff review before any commit or deploy

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Replit environment, while A is a docs-only open-source repository with no data classes touched. The pair therefore creates a compliance mismatch around sensitive data handling and retention, even though A itself is not a regulated data processor. Because the relevant residency and retention controls for B are not fully documented here, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed into the Replit workspace
IF workspace retention or export settings differ from the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use synthetic or masked test data
Confirm retention settings before upload
Document where secrets are stored
Delete temporary files after the task
